question: Why should a patient empty their bladder right before a pelvic examination?

options.A: To measure baseline kidney function accurately
options.B: To collect a routine 24-hour urine sample
options.C: To reduce pelvic discomfort and improve organ palpation
options.D: To prevent sudden drops in systemic blood pressure

explanation: Great job! An empty bladder sits lower down, making the exam much more comfortable for the patient and allowing you to feel the reproductive organs clearly. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to explain each step before starting a reproductive assessment?

options.A: To distract the patient from physical pain
options.B: To decrease patient anxiety and build trust
options.C: To speed up the total time spent in the room
options.D: To fulfill strict legal billing requirements

explanation: Spot on! Reproductive exams can feel intimidating. Explaining what you are about to do calms nerves and helps the patient trust you. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which type of lubricant must you use during a pelvic exam if a Pap smear is planned?
explanation: You got it! Petroleum or silicone jellies can mess up cellular lab samples like Pap smears. Always stick to water-soluble products. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why must speculums be either single-use plastic or properly sterilized metal?

options.A: To prevent the transmission of infections between patients
options.B: To make the examination completely painless for everyone
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital supplies
options.D: To ensure the equipment feels warm to the patient's touch

explanation: Spot on! Because these instruments touch mucous membranes, keeping them sterile or disposable stops bacteria and viruses from spreading from person to person. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h2)

question: Unexplained facial hair growth in a female patient can be a sign of which condition?
explanation: Correct! Extra facial hair (hirsutism) is often linked to higher androgen levels, which are common in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h3)

question: A male patient has enlarged breast tissue during a routine check. Which body system is likely involved?
explanation: You nailed it! Gynecomastia (enlarged male breast tissue) is usually driven by hormone imbalances, which fall under the endocrine system. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h3)

question: What position is a female patient usually placed in for a full pelvic examination?
explanation: Correct! The lithotomy position (lying on the back with legs in stirrups) gives you the best view and access for checking pelvic organs. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of bimanual palpation during a female pelvic exam?

options.A: To check for external skin lesions on the labia majora
options.B: To collect a sample of surface cells from the outer surface of the cervix
options.C: To measure the exact pH balance of vaginal fluid secretions
options.D: To evaluate the size, shape, and consistency of internal organs like the uterus

explanation: Spot on! By placing one hand inside the vagina and the other on the lower belly, you can 'sandwich' the organs to feel their size and tenderness. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which structures should you palpate when doing a routine male genital check?
explanation: You got it! Gently checking the testes and the epididymis helps you spot any lumps, swelling, or tenderness early on. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is teaching self-examination important in male reproductive care?

options.A: It is the only reliable way to diagnose a urinary tract infection
options.B: It replaces the need for any future professional medical visits
options.C: It helps patients detect early changes like lumps or swelling
options.D: It prevents the normal age-related decrease in testosterone

explanation: Correct! Self-exams empower patients to notice small changes right away, leading to quicker medical help and better health results. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of doing a routine Pap smear?

options.A: To screen for precancerous cellular changes on the cervix
options.B: To diagnose a severe bacterial urinary tract infection
options.C: To measure circulating levels of reproductive hormones
options.D: To test for active yeast infections in the vagina

explanation: Spot on! A Pap smear collects cervical cells to look for unusual changes before they have a chance to turn into cervical cancer. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which mistake during a cervical swab can ruin the lab result?

options.A: Explaining the testing procedure to the patient too early
options.B: Using a plastic speculum instead of a cold metal one
options.C: Allowing the patient to empty their bladder before the exam
options.D: Leaving excess mucus on the cervix before taking the sample

explanation: You got it! Too much mucus or discharge blocks the cells, making it impossible for the lab tech to read the sample accurately. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is a good example of objective documentation during a reproductive assessment?

options.A: Patient seems overly anxious and does not like pelvic exams
options.B: Skin intact, no lesions or abnormal discharge noted on the labia
options.C: Patient is probably hiding symptoms due to personal embarrassment
options.D: External genitalia look completely normal and healthy overall

explanation: Spot on! Objective notes focus on clear, observable facts rather than personal guesses or vague opinions. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why should nurses avoid using vague words like 'normal' when charting physical assessments?

options.A: It violates patient privacy laws to write short descriptive sentences
options.B: Patients have a legal right to erase that word from their records
options.C: Hospital computers will automatically reject entries containing that word
options.D: Different healthcare workers can interpret vague words in different ways

explanation: Correct! Using clear, descriptive details ensures every nurse or doctor reading the chart has the exact same picture of the patient's condition. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T4#GNS311_U1_T4_h7)
